security_audit.summary: Most static matches are documentation syntax, relative links, or scoped Azure checks. Confirmed risks include untrusted wrapper execution, destructive build-file handling, and credential exposure. Hidden persistent directives and unpinned external skill installation add supply-chain and agent-control risk.

remediation.issue: The BOM helper overwrites and deletes an existing rewrite.yml file.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique temporary recipe outside the project, or back up and restore any existing rewrite.yml atomically.

remediation.issue: Project wrappers and command overrides execute without a trust decision.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before wrapper execution, validate executable paths, and never add execute permission automatically.

remediation.issue: Regex-based Gradle injection and cleanup can corrupt build files.
remediation.suggestion: Use a Gradle-aware transformation, preserve exact original content, and restore atomically after failures.

remediation.issue: Function App settings and storage connection strings can reach logs or process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Do not print settings. Use identity authentication, quote all variables, and avoid connection strings on command lines.

remediation.issue: Generated templates embed hidden instructions that reject user pauses and operational limits.
remediation.suggestion: Remove persistent agent directives and require generated progress files to honor user, system, and resource limits.

remediation.issue: Redis migration skills are installed from mutable external repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed commits or signed releases, show the source to the user, and require confirmation before installation.

content.user_title: Upgrade Azure Workloads and Java SDKs
content.value_statement: Azure upgrades can fail when compatibility, identity, deployment, and rollback details are missed. This skill provides phased assessments, migration steps, validation, and recovery guidance.
actual_capabilities: Assess Linux Consumption Function Apps for Flex Consumption compatibility.
Guide app creation, configuration migration, deployment, validation, cleanup, and rollback.
Inventory legacy Azure Java SDK dependencies across Maven and Gradle projects.
Modernize com.microsoft.azure usage to supported com.azure libraries.
Resolve the latest Azure SDK BOM and apply OpenRewrite migration recipes.
Route ACR and ACRE migrations to the correct Azure Managed Redis skill.
limitations: Only documented Functions, Java, and Redis scenarios have detailed workflows.
The Flex Consumption workflow supports Linux apps and excludes unsupported platform features.
Java automation requires Python 3.10 and a Maven or Gradle project.
Azure operations require authenticated tools, adequate permissions, and user approval for resource changes.

use_cases.title: Assess a Functions Upgrade
use_cases.description: Check a Linux Consumption app for Flex compatibility before creating resources.

use_cases.title: Modernize Java Dependencies
use_cases.description: Replace unsupported Azure Java SDK packages while preserving application behavior and tests.

use_cases.title: Plan a Redis Migration
use_cases.description: Identify ACR or ACRE resources and select the correct managed Redis migration path.

prompt_templates.title: Check Flex Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether my Linux Consumption app <APP_NAME> in <RESOURCE_GROUP> can move to Flex Consumption. Do not create resources.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Functions Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Flex Consumption migration for <APP_NAME>. Include compatibility, identity, deployment, validation, rollback, and confirmation gates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Java Modernization
prompt_templates.prompt: Inventory the Java project at <PROJECT_PATH> for legacy Azure SDKs. Resolve the latest BOM and propose changes before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Execute an Approved Java Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute the approved migration for <PROJECT_PATH>. Confirm wrapper trust, apply required changes, run tests, and summarize remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Assess my Linux Consumption function app for Flex Consumption.
output: Blockers: deployment slots and polling blob triggers
Required action: convert triggers and choose a supported region
Next gate: confirm the target app before creation

output_examples.input: Plan migration from legacy Azure Java management libraries.
output: Inventory: legacy management and authentication packages found
Target: supported Azure Resource Manager and Azure Identity libraries
Validation: compile tests, run tests, and verify zero legacy references
Rollback: retain the migration branch and last successful commit

output_examples.input: Which Redis migration path applies to Enterprise_E20?
output_examples.output: Enterprise_E20 is an ACRE resource. Use the reviewed ACRE to AMR migration skill after confirming its pinned source.

best_practices: Complete assessment and rollback planning before changing Azure resources.
Use managed identity and preserve the original workload until validation succeeds.
Review wrappers, generated commands, and source changes before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not delete or stop the original workload before explicit confirmation.
Do not print app settings, connection strings, tokens, or credential files.
Do not install external migration skills from an unreviewed mutable branch.

faq.question: Does this skill migrate Windows Consumption apps?
faq.answer: No. The included Flex Consumption workflow covers Linux apps only.

faq.question: Can it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: It provides creation commands, but resource creation requires authenticated tools and explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Which Java build systems are supported?
faq.answer: The Java workflow supports Maven and Gradle, including documented version catalog variants.

faq.question: Does it perform Redis migration directly?
faq.answer: No. It identifies ACR or ACRE and routes the request to a dedicated migration skill.

faq.question: How does it protect rollback options?
faq.answer: It keeps the original workload available until the new workload passes validation and the user approves cleanup.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: Assessment needs project access and Azure read permissions. Execution also needs approved write permissions and trusted local build tools.
